provenance.method: Static team-labelled source references, independently checked against the identified downloaded source bytes before the expanded benchmark freeze.
provenance.excerpt_normalization: HTML: stdlib HTMLParser text nodes excluding scripts/styles, joined with spaces, then whitespace collapse. Excerpts are exact contiguous substrings. Multiple excerpts joined with blank lines are enumerated separately. Character offsets refer to this full normalized document text.
provenance.retrieved_at_note: No retrieval timestamp claimed; downloaded original bytes identified by SHA-256.
provenance.split_policy: Source-family split: general plate and cardiometabolic food guidance (plate, Diabetes Hub, hypertension, fats) are dev. Child/teen and maternal nutrition (children, breastfeeding, antenatal supplements) are test, consistent with existing HealthHub RDA test assignment. Related family documents remain together. Publisher and broad nutrition topics overlap; test is not a claim of unseen pretraining or independently held-out clinical validation.
provenance.source_check: All seven original HTML SHA-256 hashes and all 61 excerpt substrings and offsets independently checked against downloaded bytes. Extraction and AnswerDraft schemas, predicate evaluation, source links, splits and lexical exemplars checked locally.
provenance.pattern_checks: Bounded lexical diagnostics only; semantic review must assess negation, qualifiers, exceptions and population. Seven answerable questions selected for evidence-removal ablation.
provenance.experiment_context: The main 14-passage experiment was already run as an initial experiment. No prompts were tuned from its outputs. This expanded-reference check used source text and local schemas, with no evaluation model calls.

limitations: Team-labelled static references; not independently clinically adjudicated.
Seven HealthHub-hosted official pages (HPB, Ministry of Health, Tan Tock Seng Hospital and Pharmaceutical Society of Singapore contributions); ACE and PrimaryCarePages were not included.

Selection is source extraction and source-grounded answering, not endorsement of every source claim or proof of current clinical consensus. Historical or source-specific advice is retained as written.
No synthetic patients, observed patient outcomes or benchmark results. No RDA excerpts reused.
Family-level splitting reduces related-document leakage but does not eliminate shared publisher, cross-links, broad topic overlap or pretraining contamination.
HTML text was checked against downloaded bytes; no independent visual or clinical adjudication.
Numeric unsupported subjects, additional ranges, strict inequalities and unsupported applicability remain blocked qualitative advice rather than silently computable rules.
The breastfeeding energy article differs from RDA guidance; preserve source-specific qualifiers rather than resolving differences here.
All questions are answerable with supplied passages; evidence-removal ablation supplies the missing-evidence probe.
The breastfeeding article includes an apparently mismatched CDC reference URL outside selected passages; no corroboration through that citation is claimed.

A well-nourished breastfeeding mother will need an additional 330 to 400 kilocalories (kcal) 1 per day. This means that a breastfeeding mother should consume approximately 2,000 to 2,800 kcal per day*.

blockers: The additional action cannot encode an additional range without loss; keep the additional range and approximate total separate in advice.

limitations: Team-labelled reference; not independently clinically adjudicated.

passages.content:
What To Eat While Breastfeeding

Vitamins and supplements may not be necessary if you have a varied and balanced diet. Ensure that the foods you eat provide enough carbohydrates for energy, calcium for strong bones and protein to help your baby grow. Just continue to eat nutritious foods as advised for your pregnancy diet, and you’re all set! However, if you feel that your calcium intake and sun exposure had reduced post-delivery, you may wish to supplement with Vitamin D and calcium.

action.subject: supplements
action.advice: No. Supplements may not be necessary with a varied, balanced diet. If calcium intake and sun exposure have reduced after delivery, vitamin D and calcium supplementation may be considered.

blockers: Diet adequacy, reduced calcium intake and sun exposure are unsupported predicates; preserve conditional advice without inventing doses.

limitations: Team-labelled reference; not independently clinically adjudicated.
